── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: 7, 0, 5.1, 0 km
This week: 0 km over 0 runs. Missed 3 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "Fine, a bit stiff from all the driving."
Feeling: "Want to get going again."
Asks: "I haven't run for two weeks. Do I have to start again from the beginning? And is the 5K in four weeks still realistic?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Two weeks off costs you a little, not what you have built, so restart one step back with 2-minute running spells. …
Answers: (1) No, you don't need to start again from the beginning. … (2) Finishing the 5K on Nov 15 is realistic. Running the whole way is very unlikely, and I would not push for it. (3) Most new runners need eight or more steady weeks to close a gap like that. … (4) A walk-run with walk breaks decided in advance, such as 4 or 5 minutes running and 1 minute walking, can get you…
Next week:
Mon: easy, 26 min, 5 min brisk walk, then 7 x (2 min run, 1 min walk), running slowly…
Tue: rest. The usual dog walk is fine. Gives your legs a day to absorb the first run back.
Wed: easy, 29 min, 5 min brisk walk, then 8 x (2 min run, 1 min walk), same easy pace…
Thu: rest. The usual dog walk is fine. Recovery between runs.
Fri: rest. The usual dog walk is fine. Two quiet days set you up for the step up on…
Sat: long, 29 min, 5 min brisk walk, then 6 x (3 min run, 1 min walk), running a little…
Sun: rest. The usual dog walk is fine. Recovery before next week's longer running spells.
